Five commits by Lovable (gpt-engineer-app[bot]). Brief: `docs/tasks/T-028-l5c-public-pages.md`. Lovable's own report: `docs/external/lovable/2026-10-14-l5c-public-pages.md`.

**Checks:** the CI job `check` passed on ce5954d (e2e skipped). The reviewer could not run `bun run check` locally, because `bun install` needs the registry rewrite. The PR's Verification section is empty, and Lovable's report says nobody ran `bun run check` or `bun run build` by hand. So the CI run is the only evidence that lint, typecheck, format, tests and the generated-docs check pass.

## Findings, most severe first

### 1. Medium: the onboarding account-type selector changes behaviour

File: `src/routes/onboarding.tsx:230-253`.

- The PR adds "Rodina" / "Instituce / Organizace" buttons that call `setType(...)`.
- The comment at `onboarding.tsx:62-63` says the type is decided at sign-up (T-021), from `signup_kind`. With these buttons, it can now be changed after sign-up.
- The server does not check it. `create_account_onboarding` (`drizzle/migrations/0011_multi_account_tenancy.sql:200-204`) only checks that the value is FAMILY or INSTITUTIONAL.
- What goes wrong:
  - A user who signed up with Google taps "Instituce" and gets an INSTITUTIONAL account without going through the institution sign-up. That account gets institution features (public request form, approvals).
  - Someone who signed up as an institution taps "Rodina" and silently creates a family account.
  - Race: the effect at lines 71-77 runs again when `profile.display_name` loads. A user who tapped "Rodina" before that is switched back to INSTITUTIONAL.
- This is not a tenancy breach, because users only create their own account. It is still product/auth logic, which Lovable may not change.
- A human needs to decide: keep the selector (then fix the race and decide whether the server should check), or remove it.

### 2. Medium: the PR's own verification claims

- The Verification section is empty.
- Lovable's report says `bun run check` and `bun run build` were not run.
- CI is green, but the PR body should paste that output.

### 3. Low: `roadmap.md:5` marks unfinished items as done

It ticks "Check contrast, brands, cookie position…". Lovable's report itself says:

- The cookie banner was not checked on the invitation or other public-token pages.
- The blue brand was only previewed with a token, with no real institution account.
- The calendar's `--faint` text fails 4.5:1 contrast (2.25 and 2.28).
- The brief's breakpoint checks (375/768/1280) and per-state checks were not done everywhere.

### 4. Low: "Nahlásit neaktuální" fails silently

File: `src/routes/verejne.manual.$token.tsx`, the `flag` mutation (around lines 46-58).

It has no `onError`. If the call fails, nothing happens on screen (invariant 6). This is an older bug: the PR restyled the button but did not fix it.

### 5. Low: an onboarding save ignores errors

File: `src/routes/onboarding.tsx`, in `finish()`.

The `onboarding_answers` upsert does not check `error`. This is an older bug, but the file is in this PR's scope.

### 6. Low: signed-in users briefly see sign-in buttons

File: `src/routes/index.tsx:76-86`.

The landing screen says "Otevírám vaši chatu" ("opening your cottage"), but now also shows "Přihlásit se" and "Obnovení hesla" buttons. Signed-in users are redirected, but see these buttons until then.

### 7. Low: hero image sizes don't match the image

Files: `src/routes/index.tsx:60-61`, `src/routes/auth.tsx:270-271`.

`width={1200} height={1200}` says the image is square, but it is shown at 16:10. CSS fixes the box, so nothing jumps, but the numbers are wrong (they were 1024x640). The real photo sizes were not checked.

### 8. Low: `src/routes/__root.tsx` imports the same file twice

It imports `@/lib/i18n` at line 3 and `../lib/i18n` at line 176.

### 9. Info: the test cottage's public calendar is now switched on

Lovable switched on the public calendar link on "Testovací chata (Lovable)". That is allowed (invariant 8), but the team should know.

## What passed

- **Tenancy:** no SQL or grants changed. The public token routes call the same RPCs as before. The new og, title and description tags are fixed Czech strings with no cottage data. `noindex` is kept.
- **Supabase errors:** every Supabase call added by this PR checks `error`. No `alert()`.
- **Language and tap targets:** all new text goes through `t("cs", "en")`, Czech first. Tap targets are 44px or more.
- **Personal data:** no emails or phone numbers in the added lines.
- **Scope:** all 13 files are on the T-028 allowlist. Nothing changed in `drizzle/`, `supabase/`, `*.functions.ts`, `src/integrations`, `.env*`, `.github`, `.claude`, `docs/decisions` or `supabase/tests`. The CI job is still named `check`.
